title: Module 2: Neural Network Engineering & Eliminating Host-Device Stalls
description: Building multi-layer neural blocks (torch.nn.Module vs. Flax NNX / functional PyTrees), AdamW vs. Optax, DataLoader configuration for TPUs, and eliminating host-device synchronization stalls.

units.title: 2.1 Neural Modules, RMSNorm, SwiGLU & Optimizer State (PyTorch vs. JAX)

quiz.question: In an AdamW optimizer, how much extra TPU HBM memory is consumed by optimizer state per learnable parameter in float32?
options: 8 bytes per parameter (4 bytes for the first moment m_t + 4 bytes for the second moment v_t), doubling or tripling the memory footprint of the model weights.
quiz.explanation: AdamW maintains two exponential moving averages per weight parameter: first moment m_t (mean of gradients) and second moment v_t (uncentered variance of gradients). In float32, m_t and v_t add 8 bytes per parameter on top of the weight and gradient buffers.

quiz.question: Why should a PyTorch DataLoader feeding a Cloud TPU VM be configured with drop_last=True and num_workers=0 (or persistent spawn workers)?
options: drop_last=True prevents a smaller final batch at the end of an epoch from triggering a full XLA dynamic-shape recompilation, and num_workers=0 avoids fork() deadlocks with multithreaded libtpu.
Because TPUs cannot process more than 1 batch per epoch.
Because shuffle=True is unsupported in Python 3.12.
quiz.explanation: A remainder batch with a different batch size causes XLA to recompile the entire forward/backward graph. Additionally, POSIX fork() after initializing libtpu threads can deadlock child processes.

units.title: 2.2 Asynchronous Dispatch & Eliminating Host-Device Stalls (Detached Loss & lax.scan)

quiz.question: What happens to TPU utilization if you execute print(f'Step {step}: {loss.item()}') on every single training step?
options: It speeds up training by clearing the TPU queue.
loss.item() forces a synchronous DMA transfer from TPU HBM to Host CPU RAM on every step, draining the asynchronous execution queue and leaving the TPU idle while waiting for Python on the host.
It only prints once at the end of training.
quiz.explanation: Both TorchTPU and JAX dispatch compiled TPU kernels asynchronously so Python can enqueue Step N+1 while the TPU is still executing Step N. Calling .item() blocks the host until Step N finishes, creating a host-dispatch bubble between every step.

quiz.question: How do you log average training loss every K steps in TorchTPU without stalling the TPU on intermediate steps?
options: Accumulate running_loss += loss.detach() on the TPU device tensor across K steps, and only call running_loss.item() once when step % K == 0.
quiz.explanation: Adding loss.detach() to a TPU-resident scalar accumulator enqueues a lightweight on-device addition without copying bytes back to the host CPU until the logging interval K is reached.
